questions.prompt: What is the main responsibility of the View in MVVM?
choices: Holds business rules and validation logic
Renders the ViewModel's state and forwards user input to it
Fetches data from a database or web API
Contains the domain entities and invariants
questions.explanation: The View is dumb: it draws what the ViewModel exposes and forwards interactions back. It should never make decisions.

questions.prompt: What is the role of the ViewModel in MVVM?
choices: To render UI elements on screen
To store raw data exactly as it comes from the server
To expose state and commands from the model in a form the View can bind to
To communicate directly with the database
questions.explanation: The ViewModel is the adapter: it turns model state into presentable state and view actions into model operations.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the Model in MVVM is TRUE?
choices: It must be a MonoBehaviour attached to a GameObject
It holds the data and business logic, independent of any UI framework
It always lives in the same class as the View
It is only allowed to contain serialized fields
questions.explanation: The Model is UI-agnostic. In this game, Question and QuizSession are plain C# classes with no Unity dependencies.

questions.prompt: Which dependency direction is correct in MVVM?
choices: The ViewModel knows about the concrete View class
The View knows about the ViewModel, and the ViewModel knows about the Model
The Model references the ViewModel directly
All layers reference each other freely
questions.explanation: Dependencies point inward: View -> ViewModel -> Model. The ViewModel raises events; it never touches UI code.

questions.prompt: How does a ViewModel typically notify the View that its state changed?
choices: By directly calling methods on the View's Button
By polling the View every frame
By raising a change/notification event that the View subscribes to
By writing the new state to a file the View watches
questions.explanation: In WPF this is INotifyPropertyChanged; in Unity, plain C# events work well. QuizViewModel raises StateChanged and QuestionPresented.

questions.prompt: What is data binding in the context of MVVM?
choices: Copying files between folders during a build
A mechanism that automatically synchronizes View elements with ViewModel state
Serializing the ViewModel into JSON on every frame
Linking two GameObjects in the scene hierarchy
questions.explanation: Binding keeps the View in sync with the ViewModel. This game binds explicitly in event handlers, which is common in Unity.

questions.prompt: Why is it useful that the ViewModel has no references to UI classes?
choices: It makes the ViewModel slower but safer
It lets you unit test presentation logic without launching a UI engine
It is required by the C# language specification
It reduces the file size of the compiled game
questions.explanation: QuizViewModel can be tested in plain C# test projects because it depends only on abstractions like IQuestionRepository.

questions.prompt: What is a Domain in Domain-Driven Design?
choices: The folder where Unity stores scene files
The sphere of knowledge the software is about, e.g. quiz questions and scoring
The network protocol the game uses
Unity's name for a GameObject group
questions.explanation: The domain is the subject area. Here it's the quiz itself: questions, answers, streaks, and score rules.

questions.prompt: What is an Entity in DDD?
choices: An object with an identity that stays the same even as its data changes
Any GameObject in the Unity scene
A database table with no primary key
A UI prefab that can be instantiated
questions.explanation: An Entity has an Id and a lifecycle. Question has an Id; two Question objects with the same Id are the same question.

questions.prompt: What is a Value Object in DDD?
choices: A mutable object tracked by its database row
An immutable object defined entirely by its values, with no identity
Any C# variable of type int or float
A GameObject that never moves
questions.explanation: AnswerOutcome is a value object: two outcomes with the same values are interchangeable, and it has no identity.

questions.prompt: What is a Repository in DDD?
choices: A UI component that displays lists
An object that provides the illusion of an in-memory collection of domain objects
A Unity Asset Store package
A saved copy of the project on GitHub
questions.explanation: IQuestionRepository gives the domain collection-like access to questions, hiding where they actually come from (JSON, a server, anything).

questions.prompt: What does Ubiquitous Language mean in DDD?
choices: Using English everywhere in the codebase
Naming code elements after the words domain experts actually use
Writing comments in every supported language
Prefixing all class names with the project name
questions.explanation: When a teacher says 'streak bonus', the code says StreakBonus. Shared vocabulary between experts and developers.

questions.prompt: What is a Domain Service in DDD?
choices: A stateless operation that expresses a domain concept that doesn't naturally belong to one Entity
A background thread that syncs with a server
The MonoBehaviour that boots the game
A class that draws the UI
questions.explanation: IScorePolicy is domain-adjacent: awarding points is domain logic that isn't owned by Question or QuizSession alone.

questions.prompt: What is an Aggregate in DDD?
choices: A SQL JOIN of all tables
A cluster of domain objects treated as one unit, with one root controlling all changes
A folder of related scripts
The total sum of the player's score
questions.explanation: QuizSession acts as an aggregate root: questions, streak and score change only through its Answer method, keeping invariants safe.

questions.prompt: Where does a Repository belong in an MVVM + DDD project?
choices: In the View, next to the UI code
In the ViewModel, hard-coded as private methods
Behind an interface in the domain; the ViewModel depends on the interface
Inside the Unity scene as a GameObject
questions.explanation: The domain defines IQuestionRepository; infrastructure implements it; the ViewModel receives the interface. This is dependency inversion.

questions.prompt: Why should UI code (like MonoBehaviour) stay out of the domain and ViewModel layers?
choices: Because MonoBehaviours cannot contain logic
So those layers stay testable, portable, and independent of Unity's frame loop
Because Unity forbids classes outside the Assets folder
So the game runs faster at runtime
questions.explanation: Domain and ViewModel here compile as plain C#. You could reuse them in a console app or a WPF quiz trainer unchanged.
